translation:
I left the questioning to Koizumi, and the rest
of us went with Haruhi.

Let me guess, you can't sit still, so you're
going to jump straight to the investigation?

Of course not. Before you start an
investigation, you have to make preparations.

That doesn't sound like Haruhi. She'd sooner
run into a wall than plan a way around it.

Umm, what kind of "preparations” do you
have in mind?

Naturally, I've already thought out
everything we need to do.

For starters—Mikuru, Yuki, and Kyon, wait
here.
I'm going to be back in a bit. Got it?
O-okay.
Oi, just where are you planning to go?

Surely she doesn't mean to go investigate on
her own, right?

Prep work, just prep work. Now don't make a
fuss and just stay in this room!

I won't let you get away with it if you go
investigate without orders!
I get it.

She stole the words right out of my mouth. Is
she even going to come back?
Will Suzumiya be okay by herself?
Well… I can't really say for sure, but…
I get the feeling she'll be fine.

She's the type to openly declare what she's
going to do, after all.

I suppose you're right. Then, shall I make
some tea while we wait?
I'd be very grateful.

If I get to drink Asahina's brewed nectar, I
could wait as long as need be.
How is it?

It's truly delicious. Today's tea is excellent
yet again.

Ehe, thank you very much. Please enjoy the
rest of it.
Ahh, why of course.

Even though it's hot tea, it seeps through my
body better than cold juice would.

While I single-mindedly savored the goodness,
there was a violent knocking on the door.
Actually, maybe it was more like kicking?
What is it?
Kyon!

My hands are full, so hurry up and open the
door!
You're a genuine idiot.

When I opened the door, Haruhi fell in with a
mountain of books.

That's the first thing you say? Aren't you
going to at least thank me for letting you in?

I don't care about that trivial stuff. More
importantly, I got hold of some material.
Material? You mean this mountain of books?

Yeah. Recent history of the local area, and
material related to North High.

Wha… There's so many. Are we going to search
through these?

Of course. Before examining the crime scene,
you first need a preliminary investigation.

Hey now, I don't plan on taking extra history
classes during my summer break.

This is way more fulfilling than supplementary
classes.

You know how legends and folklore usually
have their roots in true stories?
Do they?

They do. That's why when you research ghost
stories you need to start from the source.

The history of the area, or strange incidents
involving North High and stuff.

So we'll divide the work between us and look
for clues like that!

She started shoving books at all of us with
such forcefulness that no one could object.

Well, I guess this is leagues better than
walking around the school aimlessly.

And thus, the SOS Brigade began diligently
reading, as if we'd all become Nagato.

…Well, that was the intention at least. But
what's with all the noise?
What the heck is this?!

These boulders look so meaningful, but their
origin is totally boring!

I can't believe it. I wish there were at least a
better reason than that. You know?
Eh? Ah, yes. Y-you're right~

It seems Haruhi has been completely
absorbed by entertainment articles.

Like, "Places You Can Find Boulders That
Look Like Creatures…”

Or, "An Ominous Antique Was Found in
Someone's Storehouse,” and stuff like that.

Simply binging stories that have not the least
relation to our case.

Our only hope is Nagato, who alone is ignoring
Haruhi and calmly reading on.
Have you found anything relevant, Nagato?

… At present, nothing has had significant
information recorded in it.
Oh, okay…

The material is so local to this area that it's
only natural.

We should've assumed there'd be nothing in
the first place and saved some time.

Ahaha—the advertisements in here are a
great read!

I thought Haruhi would be in a bad mood if we
couldn't find any good info, but…

She seems to be surprisingly enjoying herself,
so no problem here.

How about you, Kyon? Have you found any
funny articles?
Make sure to tell me if you find any.

Funny articles? Since when was that our main
objective?
How can I pass the time?
Asahina, how are you doing?
Huh?
Gyah?!

Asahina turned around in a panic, and her
hand knocked the teapot.

The tea spilled everywhere—even one of the
books got wet.
Are you okay, Asahina?

I'm okay, but… I got some of our documents
wet. What should I do?

Part of the paper swelled up, and the letters
started to blur, becoming unreadable.

Even if you tried to dry it, it would just
smudge.

Errr… Suzumiya… This was important, wasn't
it?

It looked like it had been stored away for
years, so it can't have been that important.

As long as you destroy the evidence, it's all
good.
And just how do you plan on doing that?

Burn it, maybe. It's fine though—they had
tons of extra copies that looked identical.

Truly the mutterings of a demon. What Haruhi
says is true, though.
I'll get rid of the book.
A [#P05stained] book[#P01], huh…

Rather than recklessly throwing it away, it'd
be safer to just keep hold of it for now.

Sorry, Nagato. You didn't find any funny
articles, did you?
…Funny articles?
She looked at me with a curious expression.

…I just asked for help on reflex, but maybe I
should've phrased the question better.

In other words, stories you read that you
thought were unique, maybe.
…This?

She slightly tilted her head as she handed
something to me. Th-this is…

It was the design document for a uniqueness
award an old North High student received.
A very literal interpretation, I guess…
…Yes.

Actually, it's technically not wrong, but it kind
of misses the point.

Kyon! Stop relying on Yuki and search for
yourself!
Yes, yes, I'm on it.

I'll keep a mental note of [#P05Nagato]'s design
document[#P01] now that I've seen it.

In the end, nothing came of my attempt to get
help. I'll just get back to reading.

By the way, since when did our objective
change to finding funny articles?

I wasn't paying any attention, so I didn't
notice.

Both Mikuru and Yuki found absolutely
hilarious articles!
For goodness' sake Kyon, you must be blind.

What?! Since when did those two find that kind
of thing?!

Neither of them acted like they had when I
just asked them.

As punishment for being the only one to not
find anything, go buy drinks.
Enough for everyone here, of course.
Why does it have to be this way?

Umm, if you're thirsty, I can make some more
tea?

I'm fine for now. Besides, it's hot today so it's
better to have juice, right?
Eh? U-um, I'm not thirsty yet, so…

Nagato had the same neutral expression as
always.

We had been reading in this hot room for a
while…

Truth be told, I was starting to drip with
sweat.

You already treated us to tea earlier. I'd be
happy to get some juice for you.

Right. If it's for Asahina's sake, such trivial
punishment is nothing.
Hey, Kyon—you better get it quick!
And it better be freezing cold! Hurry up!

I'm tempted to just buy ice and throw it at you
instead. Good grief.
Oh my, we meet at such a perfect time.
I came across Koizumi while out buying juice.

I'm not buying you anything if you turn up out
of nowhere as if it were your plan all along.

I'm fine. More importantly, there's something I
want your help with.
What might that be?

I know a way of hindering the investigation,
but it's a bit of a bother to do it by myself.

Got it. If that's what you want, I'll give you a
hand.
Then if you'd follow me…
So, what are we doing here?
Koizumi took me outside class 1-6.

Would you mind helping me take the plate that
labels this classroom?

Then we'll put class 7's plate in its place, and
shift all the class plates across.

I don't mind, but what's the point in doing all
that?
It's just an idea to set up a simple little trick.

Doing so will cause an illusion as you move
along the hallway from class 6…

The plan is to create another classroom
adjacent to 1-9.

I see. So at a glance, it'll probably appear as
if that one is class 10.

Instead of a trick, I'd say it's more on the
level of a mischievous child's cheap prank.
Indeed, but that suits our purpose.

The computer society members simply
misunderstood someone's prank…
How does that explanation sound?
Not bad, I think.

It's an elementary trick that you'd see in
mystery novels.
I believe it could buy us some time.

I agree. Let's quickly swap them out while
Haruhi isn't looking.
We got straight to preparing Koizumi's trick.
Okay, the plate is off.

What? Who would call me at a time like this?
Gah! It's not Haruhi, is it?

Don't mind me—please answer. And remember
to keep the trick a secret.
…H-hello? What's going on, Haruhi?

What's going on? You stole the words from my
mouth! How far are you going for that juice?
Did you forget I told you to be quick about it?
You genuine imbecile, Kyon!
O-oh yeah, you did say that. My bad.

Enough with the excuses! Get back here now!
In the next three seconds!

That's impossible! …Is what I would say had
she not disconnected right after telling me.

It seems that I've asked for help at a busy
time. My apologies.

Not at all—it's my fault for forgetting I was
in a hurry.

We haven't done anything but take the plate
down.
From here on, I'll do what I can on my own.

For now, it's critical to avoid dampening Miss
Suzumiya's mood too much.
Yeah, that's right.

I'd better get back quickly. Though what
should I do about the plate we removed?

I can't just leave it here, so there's no choice
but to take it with me.

It's quite bulky, but I'll take the [#P05class] 6 plate[#P01]
with me inside my blazer.

There's obviously no way I can take
something like this with me.

I'll hide it behind something until we can fix it
later.

Hm? There's something else here. An [#P05answer]
sheet[#P00] for a test?
They probably failed and hid it.
It seems old. Maybe I'll throw it out later…

Oops—if I don't get back to the clubroom
fast, I'll get another call from Haruhi.
Ask Mikuru for help
Ask Nagato for help
Carry it with you
Hide it around there
